messages:
jordan: Hey team — partner needs a custom pressure-relief wheelchair cushion, vendor is out-of-network. Fitting scheduled in 9 days and vendor says they need pre-auth or they won't ship. Claim got pended for "no prior auth." Any quick path to get approval or an exception?
tasha: Sorry you're dealing with that, Jordan. Short answer: we can request an expedited prior-authorization or a medical necessity exception. Need member ID, item code (HCPCS), and prosthetist quote. DM those and we'll kick off an expedited case.
benefits-bot: Hi Jordan — please file a pre-auth at https://benefits.redwood.example.com/preauth and include: 1) itemized quote, 2) clinician evaluation/letter of medical necessity, 3) product spec with HCPCS (e.g., E2605, E2606). Mark "Expedited" and attach the scheduled fitting date. Typical expedited turnaround: 72 hrs.
arun: If vendor is out-of-network because of specialty device, we can request a single-case agreement or network exception. I can run a geo-search for any in-network DME suppliers within 75 miles. Also ask the vendor for exact HCPCS and whether they can submit an invoice in provider name or accept direct payment.
jordan: Sending DM with member ID and quote now. Vendor attached HCPCS E2605 and a clinician note.
vendor-bill: We can accept direct billing to insurer but need payer EDI info and provider billing address. We can also submit a pre-auth packet if you email us the insurer contact.
emily: Process note: please email people-ops@redwood.com with subject "URGENT: DME pre-auth Member 7XXXXX" after you submit the form. That creates a manual case and assigns an EMR (case manager) to track vendor billing.
tasha: If we hit a denial, we should simultaneously file a pre-determination estimate so member knows expected OOP. Pre-determination + pre-auth together shortens overall time.
arun: Also request a "no adequate in-network supply" statement from vendor (one paragraph) — helps with exception. If vendor won't write one, I can generate a network lookup memo to attach.
jordan: Vendor just sent a short access statement and can direct-bill. Uploaded both to the pre-auth form and mailed people-ops.
tasha: Great — here's a quick vendor email template (paste vendor-specific fields):

```
To: providerrelations@insurer.example.com
Subject: Urgent pre-authorization request — Member 7XXXXX — Custom cushion fitting [YYYY-MM-DD]
Member: [Full name], DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY], Member ID: 7XXXXX
Supplier: [Vendor name], NPI: [#####], HCPCS: [E2605]
Service date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
Attachments: itemized quote, supplier access statement, clinician letter of medical necessity
Request: expedited pre-auth AND pre-determination; request direct billing to insurer. Please confirm receipt and provide EDI payer details if accepted.
```

emily: I'll take the manual case and send vendor EDI to vendor-bill. If insurer doesn't respond in 48 hrs, we'll escalate to provider relations and mark as urgent for clinical review.
vendor-bill: Received — we'll prep claim/estimate once we have payer EDI. Please advise on billing NPI to use; we can bill under vendor or clinician per payer preference.
jordan: One more Q — if we end up paying OOP before insurer finalizes, can we submit to FSA/HSA?
tasha: Yes — durable medical equipment is typically eligible for HSA/FSA. Save receipts and EOBs. If insurer later covers, you'll get EOB adjustments.
emily: Case created: DME-PA-2026-441. Assigned to emily. Expedited ETA 72 hrs. I'll post insurer ack here.
arun: Running network search now; will share a short memo if we have any in-network suppliers close by.
jordan: Thanks all — vendor could do direct bill, so fingers crossed. Will update once insurer replies. :heart:
